result.topicName: Event loop, call stack, microtasks vs macrotasks

answers.3: When the function is invoked, a execution context is pushed into the call stack, with its variable environments, lexical environments and this (context). Here the code within the function is executed line by line from top to bottom. In-case a synchronous child-function call is tumbled upon, it pushed it into the stack to get it executed. Once the child-function done execution it is popped and the parent code resumes execution. Lets say a asynchronous function comes over, then the function is invoked, and the code execution continues. Basically the call-stack works as a reference to track the execution flow. It works based on LIFO model.
answers.8: React leverages message channel to yield back to browser because, only  1 macro task  is picked in an event tick. This gives react a reliable way of knowing when the control is sent back. Since micro tasks do not have this criteria, they can be picked up during anytime. Thus making it difficult keep track of browser vsync cycles
